citation: X. Zhang, Y. Sugano, M. Fritz, A. Bulling. "It's Written All Over Your Face: Full-Face Appearance-Based Gaze Estimation." CVPR Workshops (CVPRW), 2017.
X. Zhang, Y. Sugano, M. Fritz, A. Bulling. "Appearance-Based Gaze Estimation in the Wild." CVPR, 2015.
number_format: every number is rounded to 10 significant digits, and any number smaller than 1e-09 in size is written as 0, so that last-digit floating-point noise is very unlikely to change the file between runs on the same cache with the same libraries (environment); it is not impossible, and other library builds can differ further

sections.feature_sanity: a. Are the iris offsets sane? Ranges per eye, whether both eyes move together, whether both eyes' x offsets have the same sign against the target's x, and the EyeOS roll spread. One eye's axis mirrored (its corners labelled the wrong way round) shows as target_x_signs_match false; an iris paired with the other eye's corners shows as x_medians_within_eye false (a median x of several half-widths; a healthy one is well inside +-1), while the sign check still passes.
sections.in_sample_ceiling: b. How well could one calibration of these features do across all of a person's days? Each model is fitted on all of a person's valid frames, from every day, and scored on the same frames: about the lowest error a single affine map reaches in the cross_day setting, an optimistic bound, not a result. It does not bound a calibration made within one sitting: a per-day offset (sitting, lighting, a per-day landmark bias) raises it, yet a per-day calibration absorbs it. per_day fits each day within_day uses on that day's own frames: the bound for a per-sitting calibration. Gate 2 judges another number, the leave-one-out RMS over the calibration images (cross_day.validation_error_px, within_day.validation_error_px_mean).
sections.constant_baselines: c. What does a model that ignores the eyes score? A yardstick for every other pixel number. These are in-sample constant baselines over all valid frames (the own mean target is taken from those same frames), not a constant baseline run through the protocol and scored on its test frames only, so the two can differ.
sections.cross_day: d. The standard protocol, exactly as `evaluate` runs it for the shipping `eyeos` variant: K images per dot chosen from all of a person's frames (so from many days), tested on every other frame. The reference for within_day.
sections.within_day: d. The same protocol inside one day folder at a time: K images per dot chosen only from that day, tested on that day's other images. It is compared with cross_day's error on the frames of the same days (cross_day_mean_px_on_used_days), not on every frame: days with too few images are left out of both. Within-day far below cross-day means drift between sittings is a large share of the error, which a live session (calibrated in the same sitting) would not have; both high means drift between days is not the main cause, and in_sample_ceiling.per_day says whether any affine calibration within a day could do better. A day can hold several sittings, and a day's calibration images lie further from the dots (see calibration_mean_distance_px), so this is not a live session either.
sections.error_by_head_pose: e. Under the cross-day protocol, does the error grow as the head pose moves away from the calibration pose, and what is it on the frames Gate 2 would let through (within its head-pose limit)? The delta is Gate 2's own: the largest per-axis difference of EyeOS's yaw, pitch and roll from the calibration frames' mean, in EyeOS's degrees, whose scale head_pose_agreement checks.
sections.head_pose_agreement: f. Does EyeOS's simplified head pose track the dataset's own? EyeOS yaw, pitch and roll are regressed on the dataset's (convention in notes.dataset_head_pose): |slope| is the scale of EyeOS's degrees (1 = real degrees), r how well it follows. The sign of a slope depends on how the dataset labels its head axes and is not interpreted; the correlation matrix (all 9 pairs) shows any axis mix-up.
sections.variance_split: g. Of what the shipping model's all-days in-sample fit (in_sample_ceiling.both_eyes) leaves over, how much do the dataset's head pose and the day explain (linear least squares, R^2 over both screen axes)? Read the _beyond_target shares. Noisy iris offsets shrink the fit toward the centre, so its residual grows with the target (r2_target), and anything that follows the target, such as a head that turns toward where the eyes look, explains part of it with no head effect on the iris offsets at all: a high raw r2_head_pose alone proves nothing. High r2_head_pose_beyond_target = head motion the iris offsets do not account for; high r2_day_beyond_target = something constant within a day but different between days (sitting, lighting, a per-day landmark bias); both low = per-frame landmark noise, or effects not linear in these regressors. Plain R^2: k regressors unrelated to the residual score about k/n (n frames) by chance.

metrics.n_images: images of this person in the dataset
metrics.n_valid: images that Gate 1 would pass (exactly one face, both irises visible)
metrics.skipped: why a section could not be computed for this person
metrics.feature_sanity.left_iris_x: EyeOS left-eye iris offset along the eye's corner line, in eye half-widths: median, p5, p95 over the valid frames
metrics.feature_sanity.left_iris_y: EyeOS left-eye iris offset across the corner line (down = +), in eye half-widths: median, p5, p95
metrics.feature_sanity.right_iris_x: as left_iris_x, for the right eye (the eye on the image's right)
metrics.feature_sanity.right_iris_y: as left_iris_y, for the right eye
metrics.feature_sanity.corr_left_right_x: Pearson correlation of the two eyes' x offsets; both eyes turn together, so near +1 is healthy and noise pulls it toward 0
metrics.feature_sanity.corr_left_right_y: Pearson correlation of the two eyes' y offsets
metrics.feature_sanity.corr_left_x_target_x: Pearson correlation of the left eye's x offset with the target's x
metrics.feature_sanity.corr_right_x_target_x: Pearson correlation of the right eye's x offset with the target's x
metrics.feature_sanity.target_x_signs_match: whether both eyes' x offsets correlate with the target's x with the same sign (false = one eye's x runs the wrong way: its axis is mirrored)
metrics.feature_sanity.x_medians_within_eye: whether both eyes' median x offset lies inside the eye (|median| < 1 half-width); false = an iris paired with the wrong eye's corners, or a broken eye
metrics.feature_sanity.corr_left_y_target_y: Pearson correlation of the left eye's y offset with the target's y
metrics.feature_sanity.corr_right_y_target_y: Pearson correlation of the right eye's y offset with the target's y
metrics.feature_sanity.eyeos_roll_deg: EyeOS head roll (from the eye corners), degrees: median, p5, p95; a few degrees is expected for someone sitting at a laptop
metrics.in_sample_ceiling.both_eyes: the shipping calibration's model (affine in the 4 iris offsets, its ridge strength) fitted on all valid frames from every day: mean_px and rms_px of the rounded, clamped prediction's error, and r2_x, r2_y of the raw fit per screen axis
metrics.in_sample_ceiling.left_eye_only: as both_eyes, on the left eye's 2 offsets alone
metrics.in_sample_ceiling.right_eye_only: as both_eyes, on the right eye's 2 offsets alone
metrics.in_sample_ceiling.with_head_pose: as both_eyes, with EyeOS's yaw, pitch and roll added, fitted like the with-head-pose variant (standardised ridge)
metrics.in_sample_ceiling.per_day: the both_eyes model fitted separately on each day within_day uses, on that day's valid frames, and scored on them: days (how many), mean_px and rms_px (each the mean over those days of that day's value); null without such a day
metrics.constant_baselines.screen_centre_mean_px: mean px error of always predicting the screen centre, over all valid frames (not the protocol's test frames)
metrics.constant_baselines.own_mean_target_mean_: mean px error of always predicting this person's mean target over all valid frames, scored on all valid frames (an in-sample constant)
metrics.cross_day.n_calibration: calibration images (K per dot x 9 dots)
metrics.cross_day.n_test: test images: every other valid image
metrics.cross_day.mean_px: mean px error on the test images (as evaluate's pixel_error_px.mean)
metrics.cross_day.mean_deg: mean angular error in degrees (null without a trusted screen model)
metrics.cross_day.validation_error_px: the calibration's own leave-one-out RMS error, what Gate 2 checks
metrics.cross_day.passes_gate2: whether validation_error_px is below Gate 2's limit
metrics.cross_day.calibration_mean_distance_px: mean distance from the calibration images' true targets to their dots
metrics.cross_day.calibration_days: distinct day folders among the calibration images (null without day folders)
metrics.within_day.days_total: day folders with at least one valid image
metrics.within_day.days_used: days with at least the minimum number of valid images (config.min_day_images, and always K x 9 + 1), each calibrated and tested on its own
metrics.within_day.days_skipped: days with too few valid images (listed in skipped_days)
metrics.within_day.mean_px: mean over the days used of each day's mean px test error
metrics.within_day.mean_deg: mean over the days used of each day's mean angular error
metrics.within_day.validation_error_px_mean: mean over the days used of each day's leave-one-out validation error (Gate 2's input)
metrics.within_day.gate2_passed_days: days whose validation error is below Gate 2's limit
metrics.within_day.calibration_mean_distance_px_: mean over the days used of the calibration images' mean distance to their dots
metrics.within_day.cross_day_mean_px: cross_day.mean_px again (every test frame, skipped days included), null when no day was used, so the aggregate compares the two protocols on the same persons
metrics.within_day.cross_day_mean_px_on_used_day: mean over the days used of cross_day's mean px on that day's test frames: the standard protocol on the same days as within_day.mean_px
metrics.within_day.within_over_cross_mean_px: within_day.mean_px / cross_day_mean_px_on_used_days (both over the same days): well below 1 = drift between days matters
metrics.within_day.per_day: one entry per day used: day, n_valid, the cross_day metrics for that day's own calibration, and cross_day_mean_px, the standard calibration's mean px on that day's test frames
metrics.within_day.skipped_days: the days not used, with their number of valid images
metrics.aggregate.within_day.gate2_passed_days_t: days whose calibration passes Gate 2, summed over persons
metrics.error_by_head_pose.bins: per head-pose delta bin ([0, 5], (5, 10], (10, 15], (15, 20], (20, inf) degrees): lo_deg, hi_deg (null = open), n test frames and their mean_px
metrics.error_by_head_pose.within_limit_share: share of test frames within Gate 2's head-pose limit (evaluate's head_pose_within_limit_share)
metrics.error_by_head_pose.within_limit_mean_px: mean px error over the test frames within the limit only: what Gate 2 would act on
metrics.error_by_head_pose.beyond_limit_mean_px: mean px error over the test frames beyond the limit (null if there are none)
metrics.head_pose_agreement.dataset_axes_relabel: which half turn of the dataset's head frame was undone first ('none' = used as stored)
metrics.head_pose_agreement.dataset_pose_median_: median dataset yaw, pitch and roll over the valid frames, in degrees
metrics.head_pose_agreement.yaw: EyeOS yaw regressed on the dataset's yaw: slope (EyeOS degrees per real degree), intercept (degrees) and Pearson r; null when either does not vary
metrics.head_pose_agreement.correlation_matrix: Pearson r of each EyeOS angle (eyeos_*) with each dataset angle (dataset_*)
metrics.variance_split.residual_rms_px: RMS of the raw in-sample residual being split, in px (the shipping model on all frames)
metrics.variance_split.r2_target: the control: share of the residual's variance explained by the true target (x, y) itself; high when noise has shrunk the fit toward the centre; null when the residual is below half a pixel RMS
metrics.variance_split.r2_head_pose: raw share of the residual's variance explained by the dataset's head yaw, pitch, roll (degrees, as head_pose_agreement reads them) and translation (mm); counts head pose that merely follows the target; null without head pose or when the residual is below half a pixel RMS
metrics.variance_split.r2_head_pose_beyond_targe: R^2 on target + head pose minus r2_target: what head pose explains beyond the target, the share to read as head motion
metrics.variance_split.r2_day: raw share explained by the day folder alone (between-day variance over total); null without days or when the residual is below half a pixel RMS
metrics.variance_split.r2_day_beyond_target: R^2 on target + day minus r2_target: what the day explains beyond the target
metrics.variance_split.r2_head_pose_and_day: raw share explained by head pose and day together
metrics.aggregate.error_by_head_pose.bins: the bins over all persons: n (frames), pooled_mean_px (over those frames), mean_of_person_means_px and persons (with at least one frame in the bin)

aggregate_note: aggregate.<section>.<metric> summarises the per-person metric of the same name: mean, median, min and max over the persons where it is not null (persons counts them); a true/false metric counts the persons where it is true; a text metric counts persons per value. Each person weighs the same.

notes.loading: Each image's day is the folder of its path in the extract cache's image column (dayNN). The extract cache does not keep the dataset's head pose, so head_rvec and head_tvec are read again from pXX.txt under --root and matched to the cache by image path (a cached image missing from pXX.txt, or with another target there, is an error).
notes.in_sample: in_sample_ceiling and variance_split fit on every valid frame and score on the same frames. in_sample_ceiling bounds one affine calibration of these features used across all of a person's days (the cross_day setting); in_sample_ceiling.per_day bounds one calibration per day folder (the within_day setting); variance_split says where the all-days leftover comes from. They are not a result and use the test frames.
notes.protocol: cross_day, within_day and error_by_head_pose run protocol.evaluate_person with the shipping `eyeos` variant and the run's K, so cross_day reproduces evaluate's eyeos numbers for the same cache and K (to the 10 significant digits kept here).
notes.dataset_head_pose: R = Rodrigues(head_rvec) maps the dataset's head frame to camera coordinates (x right, y down, z away from the camera). yaw = atan2(R[0,2], R[2,2]), pitch = asin(-R[1,2]), roll = atan2(R[1,0], R[1,1]) in degrees, i.e. R = Ry(yaw) Rx(pitch) Rz(roll), so a rotation about the camera's y, x or z axis reads as yaw, pitch or roll alone. If the person's mean R is closer to a half turn about one head axis than to the identity (the head frame's axes are labelled the other way round), that half turn is undone first and named in dataset_axes_relabelled. This reading has not been checked against the real files: dataset_pose_median_deg near 0 for someone facing the camera supports it, and correlation_matrix shows a mix-up.
notes.environment: where diagnose ran (Python, platform, numpy, scipy, OpenCV and MediaPipe versions; null = not found), and under `extract` what each person's landmark cache was made with, from the cache's manifest.json (null for a cache without a manifest). diagnose does not run MediaPipe itself: the landmarks come from the extract cache.
notes.eyeos_head_pose: EyeOS's head pose is its own simplified estimate (eyeos.features: landmark ratios scaled to 'degrees'), the one Gate 2 uses; head_pose_agreement measures its scale.
